text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU hotpath pool us-west-2 is at 98% utilization for 6m, queue depth rising >10k, 5xx/429 spike detected. paging oncall: alice (oncall).

alice (oncall): taking pager. can folks drop quick metrics? :eyes:

bench-bot: hotpath_pool_active=152, queue_length=10420, 429_rate=0.18, avg_latency_p95=1200ms, autoscaler.heartbeat_lag=14s

mike (runtime): seeing a lot of tokenbucket drops in logs: `token_drop pool=hotpath tier=standard reason=token_shortage rate=350/s` — also a handful of `autoscaler: missed-heartbeat` around the same time.

sara (infra): checking autoscaler pods — a couple of controllers are CrashLooping in us-west-2. running `kubectl get pods -n redwood-autoscale | grep us-west-2` gives `autoscaler-7f8d9 CrashLoopBackOff` on node `g4dn-2x`

alice (oncall): ok; priorities: 1) mitigate customer impact (reduce 429s), 2) stabilize autoscaler, 3) root cause for tokenbucket mismatch. any quick config we can flip?

mike (runtime): I suspect a ratepolicy/tier mismatch. Recent rollout last night changed token_window_ms and burst for premium tiers. Looks like premium had wider window so it grabbed shared tokens, starving standard-tier queues when hotpool is saturated (priority inversion).

julia (CSRE): customers reporting increased error rates on inference calls, some page noise. CS has notified a handful of alerted accounts. We should scope which tenants affected (high-throughput vs normal).

len (product): can we do a fast fallback to smaller quant model or CPU for low-priority requests? Might be faster than scaling GPUs.

mike (runtime): quick mitigations I propose (in order):
1) throttle premium-tier burst back to pre-rollout values (`rate-config set tier=premium burst=1.2 token_window_ms=1000`)
2) temporarily increase hotpath_pool max_replicas from 50 -> 80 (manual scale)
3) enable model-variant fallback for `tier=standard` to `mistral-quant-cpu` for non-critical requests.

alice (oncall): doing step 1 now. mike, can you prepare the exact CLI? I don't want typos.

mike (runtime): running:```
infra-cli rate-config update --pool hotpath --tier premium --burst 1.0 --token_window_ms 1000
infra-cli rate-config update --pool hotpath --tier standard --burst 0.8 --token_window_ms 1000
```
Applying...

bench-bot: rate-config applied; new effective refill rates: premium=400/s->220/s, standard=250/s->200/s

alice (oncall): step 1 done. monitoring impact.

(2m later)

bench-bot: queue_length=7200, 429_rate=0.09, p95=980ms — trending down but still elevated

sara (infra): autoscaler pod `autoscaler-7f8d9` back up after restart — root cause: leader-election deadlock after kube-apiserver transient error. I've rotated controller to standby and it's recovering. Manual scale available.

alice (oncall): ok moving to step 2. sara, please increase max_replicas to 80 and trigger backfill.

sara (infra): `kubectl scale deployment hotpath --replicas=80 -n inference` -> scaling started. backfill hooks engaged.

bench-bot: replicas=80 in 90s, queue_length=3500, 429_rate=0.03, p95=420ms

julia (CSRE): sending customer note to affected customers: "We observed transient 429s due to capacity pressure; mitigations applied, service is stabilizing. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline."

len (product): nice. any spike in cost because of manual scale? note for billing/finance.

alice (oncall): yes alert on spend, but priority is availability. we'll record cost delta.

mike (runtime): about root cause: the rollout last night updated `token_window_ms` and `burst_multiplier` in the tier policy. Looks like premium had longer window and effectively hoarded tokens during high tail-latency sequences. Combined with autoscaler heartbeat miss we had a capacity shortage and packet loss. This is a classic tokenbucket priority inversion.

alice (oncall): do we have evidence of token rebalancing failure? any metrics for token leak/unequalization?

bench-bot: token_balance_hotpath: premium=+120k tokens, standard=-98k tokens over last 10m. token_leak_events=0.

mike (runtime): yep — tokens are staying in premium queue because its `window_ms` is bigger; standard can't borrow. Fix is either reduce premium window or add cross-tier emergency buffer.

sara (infra): created a short-term rule to allow emergency borrow: `infra-cli rate-config update --pool hotpath --emergency_borrow_enabled true --borrow_ratio 0.2` — applied.

bench-bot: emergency borrow applied; tokens redistributed. queue draining.

alice (oncall): observed customer impact: ~15 tenant IDs had >1% 429s in last 30m; two customers had 5xx retries and escalated. Julia, please get list and owners.

julia (CSRE): collecting tenant list now. pinging ENG for any per-customer mitigation (e.g., route to dedicated capacity)

len (product): follow-up: we need a guardrail in rollouts to prevent `token_window_ms` changes without canarying on hotpath traffic. Also add telemetry for token imbalance alerts.

mike (runtime): agreed. Action items: 1) rollback premium token_window_ms change in config history to last known-good (I have the diff). 2) add imbalance alert when |token_balance| > X for 5m. 3) postmortem to cover autoscaler heartbeat resiliency.

alice (oncall): creating incident doc now. preliminary severity: Sev2 (customer-facing but mitigated within 30m).

(1h later)

bench-bot: tail logs show stable behavior, queue_length steady ~400, 429_rate=0.005, p95=120ms

sara (infra): autoscaler controllers healthy after image roll and leader rotation. Root cause for crashloop tracked to GC bump + leader-election race under api-server high latency; will land a fix.

mike (runtime): config rollback performed for premium tier; verified that token_window_ms restored to previous values. Also added emergency borrow feature as temporary safety.

julia (CSRE): updated customers with "service restored, we applied mitigations; follow-up RCA to be shared"; set expectation for formal RCA within 72h.

alice (oncall): final notes:
- Mitigations applied: ratepolicy rollback, emergency borrow toggle, manual scale to 80 replicas, autoscaler controllers restarted.
- Impact: transient 429s for ~45min, small # of customers escalated, service restored and stable.
- Next steps: runbook update for tokenbucket rollouts, add imbalance alert, autoscaler leader-election hardening, cost reconciliation for manual scaling.

len (product): assign owners for next steps?

mike (runtime): I'll take tokenbucket canary guard and imbalance alert.

sara (infra): I'll own autoscaler leader-election fix and deploy test.

julia (CSRE): I'll follow up with customer comms and impacted tenant table.

alice (oncall): thanks team. leaving this thread for postmortem drafting. :white_check_mark: Closing incident for now.

(reacted with :thumbsup: by mike (runtime), sara (infra), julia (CSRE))
